items.title: Section: The Parable of Medicine Opens — Curing One Disease Only to Discover a Deeper One Still Concealed Beneath It

items.zh: 又如病者往大醫所，為除病故，求隨順藥，得已常服。彼於是藥深生勝解、深生愛樂、唯見為實。由是因緣，先病除愈，復起餘病，應服餘藥。爾時大醫知先病愈，後病復生，更須餘藥；勸捨前藥，令服餘藥。時彼病者愚癡無識，於前所服深生勝解，起所宜想，不肯棄捨。
items.en: Furthermore, suppose a sick person goes to a great physician and, in order to remove their illness, seeks medicine suited to it, and, upon obtaining it, takes it constantly. This person develops deep conviction in this medicine, deep fondness for it, seeing it as genuinely effective. Because of this, the former illness is thereby cured, yet a further illness then arises, requiring a different medicine. At that time, the great physician, knowing that the former illness has been cured but a later illness has now arisen requiring a different medicine, advises abandoning the earlier medicine in favour of the one now needed. But this sick person, foolish and lacking understanding, holds deep conviction in what was taken before, believing it still suitable, and refuses to give it up.

items.title: Section: The Medicine Parable Closes — a Patient Who Hears the Physician's Correct Diagnosis Yet Still Cannot Quite Let Go

items.zh: 時大良醫為其宣說前後藥性，於現所病前藥匪宜，後藥為勝。時有病者雖聞是語，不生勝解，猶未深信良醫所言。如是病者，喻諸凡夫、菩薩、聲聞，為煩惱病之所執持。大良醫者，喻諸如來。其良藥等，喻為宣說若上上勝及以上極，若深深勝及以深極，若劣、若勝及以勝極，法教正教教授教誡。彼雖聞已，不能悟入，不生勝解，不能修行法隨法行。
items.en: At that time, the great physician explains to the patient the properties of the earlier and later medicines — that, for the illness now actually present, the earlier medicine is unsuited while the later medicine is superior. At that time, though the sick person hears these words, no genuine conviction arises, and they still do not deeply trust what the great physician has said. This sick person represents ordinary bodhisattvas and śrāvakas still gripped by the disease of affliction. The great physician represents the various tathāgatas. The good medicine represents teaching that is superior, more superior, and utterly superior; that is profound, more profound, and utterly profound; and that is lesser, greater, and utterly excellent — teaching, correct instruction, guidance, and admonishment. Though they have heard this, they are unable to enter into it, unable to give rise to genuine conviction, and unable to practise in proper accordance with the teaching.

items.title: Section: Genuine Faith Never Doubts — Why a Noble One Who Has Actually Realised the Path Can Never Mistake the Great Vehicle for Anything Less Than the Buddha's Own Word

items.zh: 諸有淨信菩薩、聲聞，於佛所說不生疑惑；乘佛所說喻如一切支具圓滿妙莊嚴車無上法乘，如善御者，隨所行地、隨所應到，疾疾進趣，無所稽留。
items.en: Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas who possess genuinely pure faith never give rise to doubt regarding what the Buddha has taught; relying on what the Buddha has taught is like riding an unsurpassed vehicle of the teaching, a wondrously adorned chariot complete with every one of its parts, and, like a skilled driver, advancing swiftly towards wherever one travels and wherever one is meant to arrive, without ever being delayed.

items.title: Section: Chapter Eighteen Opens — the Qualities of a Bodhisattva, the Final Chapter of the Initial Yoga Foundation

items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter eighteen: the qualities of a bodhisattva. What are the qualities a bodhisattva actually possesses?

items.title: Section: The First Summary Verse Opens — Five Truly Astonishing Qualities No Other Being Shares

items.zh: 嗢拕南曰：希奇、不希奇、平等心、饒益、報恩、與欣讚、不虛加行性。謂諸菩薩，於其無上正等覺乘勤修學時，應知有五甚希奇法。何等為五？一者、於諸有情非有因緣而生親愛；二者、唯為饒益諸有情故，常處生死，忍無量苦；三者、於多煩惱難復有情，善能解了調伏方便；四者於極難解真實義理，能隨悟入；五者、具不思議大威神力。如是五種菩薩所有甚希奇法，不與一切餘有情共。
items.en: A summary verse states: "Astonishing, not astonishing; a mind of equanimity, benefiting beings; repaying kindness and rejoicing in praise; a nature whose effort is never wasted." When bodhisattvas diligently train in the vehicle of supreme, correct awakening, one should understand there are five truly astonishing qualities. What are these five? First, feeling genuine affection towards beings without any prior personal connection. Second, purely for the sake of benefiting beings, constantly dwelling within birth and death, enduring boundless suffering. Third, possessing genuine skill in understanding the means of taming beings whose affliction runs deep and resists correction. Fourth, being able to penetrate directly into truths of the most extreme difficulty and subtlety. Fifth, possessing inconceivable, majestic spiritual power. These five truly astonishing qualities belong to bodhisattvas alone, shared with no other being whatsoever.

items.title: Section: Five Qualities That Look Ordinary Yet Are Secretly Astonishing — Finding Genuine Joy in Suffering Undertaken Purely for Others

items.zh: 又諸菩薩成就五種不希奇法，而名成就甚希奇法。何等為五？謂諸菩薩，以因利他苦，即為自己樂；是故菩薩恒遍受行因利他苦。是名菩薩成就第一不希奇法，而名成就甚希奇法。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas accomplish five kinds of quality that are not astonishing, yet are called accomplishing truly astonishing qualities. What are these five? Bodhisattvas who take the very suffering that comes from benefiting others as their own genuine happiness, and who therefore constantly and thoroughly undergo and sustain the suffering that comes from benefiting others — this is called a bodhisattva's accomplishment of the first not-astonishing quality, yet called accomplishing a truly astonishing quality.

items.title: Section: Choosing Rebirth Over Nirvāṇa's Own Peace, and Choosing to Teach Over Silence's Own Sweetness — With Zhiyi's Own Touching Self-Assessment

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，雖善了知生死過失、涅槃功德，而樂普令有情清淨，即為己樂；是故菩薩為淨有情增上力故，誓受生死。是名菩薩成就第二不希奇法，而名成就甚希奇法。又諸菩薩，雖善了知默然樂味，而樂普令有情清淨，即為己樂；是故菩薩為淨有情增上力故，恒勤方便為說正法，是名菩薩成就第三不希奇法，而名成就甚希奇法。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, though genuinely understanding the faults of birth and death and the merits of nirvāṇa, take joy in universally purifying beings, treating this as their own genuine happiness; therefore, driven by the heightened aspiration to purify beings, they vow to undergo birth and death. This is called a bodhisattva's accomplishment of the second not-astonishing quality, yet called accomplishing a truly astonishing quality. Furthermore, bodhisattvas, though genuinely understanding the sweet taste of silent bliss, take joy in universally purifying beings, treating this as their own genuine happiness; therefore, driven by the heightened aspiration to purify beings, they constantly and diligently seek skilful means to teach the true dharma. This is called a bodhisattva's accomplishment of the third not-astonishing quality, yet called accomplishing a truly astonishing quality.

items.title: Section: Giving Without Seeking Any Return, and Making Others' Benefit Genuinely Indistinguishable From One's Own — Closing the First Two Groups of Seven

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，雖積集六波羅蜜多所有善根，而樂普令有情清淨，即為己樂；是故菩薩為淨有情增上力故，以淨意樂施諸有情，然不希求施果異熟。是名菩薩成就第四不希奇法，而名成就甚希奇法。又諸菩薩，以利他事為自利事；是故菩薩恒現受行一切有情利益之事。是名菩薩成就第五不希奇法，而名成就甚希奇法。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, though having accumulated the wholesome roots of all six perfections, take joy in universally purifying beings, treating this as their own genuine happiness; therefore, driven by the heightened aspiration to purify beings, they give to beings with a genuinely purified aspiration, yet never seek the ripened fruit of that giving for themselves. This is called a bodhisattva's accomplishment of the fourth not-astonishing quality, yet called accomplishing a truly astonishing quality. Furthermore, bodhisattvas take the work of benefiting others as identical to the work of benefiting themselves; therefore, they constantly and willingly take up the task of benefiting every being. This is called a bodhisattva's accomplishment of the fifth not-astonishing quality, yet called accomplishing a truly astonishing quality.

items.title: Section: Equanimity of Mind Opens — Five Marks From Sharing the Very Wish for Buddhahood to Loving Every Being as an Only Child

items.zh: 又諸菩薩由五種相，當知普於一切有情其心平等。何等為五？一者、菩薩最初發心，願大菩提，如是亦為利益一切諸有情故，起平等心。二者、菩薩於諸有情住哀愍俱平等之心。三者、菩薩於諸有情，深心發起一子愛俱平等之心。四者、菩薩於從眾緣已生諸行，知是所想有情事已，知一有情所有法性，即是一切有情法性；以法平等俱行之心，於諸有情住平等心。五者、菩薩如於一有情行利益行，於一切有情行利益行，亦復如是。以利俱心，於諸有情住平等心。由此五相，是諸菩薩於諸有情其心平等。
items.en: Furthermore, one should understand that bodhisattvas, through five marks, hold a mind of equanimity universally towards all sentient beings. What are these five? First, when bodhisattvas first arouse the mind, wishing for great awakening, they likewise, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, give rise to a mind of equanimity. Second, bodhisattvas dwell in a mind joined with compassion, equanimous towards all beings. Third, bodhisattvas, with a profoundly sincere mind, give rise to a mind of equanimity joined with the love of an only child, extended to all beings. Fourth, bodhisattvas, regarding conditioned activities arisen from manifold conditions, having recognised these as the very beings they wish to benefit, know that the nature belonging to any one being is identical to the nature belonging to every being; with a mind joined with this equanimity regarding shared nature, they dwell in equanimity towards all beings. Fifth, exactly as bodhisattvas undertake beneficial action towards one being, so too do they undertake beneficial action towards all beings equally; with a mind joined with benefit, they dwell in equanimity towards all beings. Through these five marks, bodhisattvas hold a mind of equanimity towards all sentient beings.

blocks.text: A second parable, about medicine, closes the factors-of-awakening chapter. Then chapter eighteen, the qualities of a bodhisattva, the last chapter of the first part of the Bodhisattva Ground.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the earlier medicine is the two-vehicle teaching, the later the Mahāyāna; the shallow illness is the obstruction of afflictions, the deep one the cognitive obstruction. The afflictive obstruction has been removed, but only the Mahāyāna medicine of the selflessness of phenomena removes the deeper one.
Venerable Miào Jìng: these are followers unwilling to turn from the small to the great.

subs.head: A noble one does not doubt

blocks.text: Riding the Buddha's teaching is like an unsurpassed vehicle, a wondrously adorned chariot, with a skilled driver "advancing swiftly without delay". Master Cháng Bǎi: arhats never deny the Buddha; to say the Mahāyāna is not the Buddha's word would deny the two vehicles too, for without a buddha how could they exist? Venerable Miào Jìng: those with the four fruits definitely believe in the Mahāyāna, because of their wisdom.

"First, feeling affection towards beings without any prior connection." Venerable Miào Jìng: not because they are my father or mother. Master Cháng Bǎi: from the first resolve the bodhisattva takes all beings as family. (He also notes: the chapter is built on five summary verses.)

"Bodhisattvas take the suffering from benefiting others as their own happiness." Venerable Miào Jìng: suffering among beings is ordinary; not tiring of it and finding joy in it is astonishing. Master Cháng Bǎi: like loving parents for whom any hardship for their children is sweet.

Master Cháng Bǎi links this to the ninth ground and quotes Zhiyi, founder of the Tiantai school: "I hoped to reach the copper wheel, but leading a community too early, harming myself to benefit others, I reached only the iron wheel."
Venerable Miào Jìng: one thinks, "My time is precious, I must sit; how can I spend it helping others?" The bodhisattva, with prajñā, sees nothing to grasp in either.
Venerable Miào Jìng: with two sons one might treat one better; love for an only child has no such unevenness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the sūtras say the Buddha regards all beings equally as his son Rāhula.

Zhiyi was one of the greatest teachers in Chinese Buddhism, yet he judged that teaching others too early had cost his own practice. Both lecturers hold this up not as a warning against teaching, but as an example of how much a bodhisattva will give up.

quiz.q: In the medicine parable, how do the lectures map the earlier and later medicines?
options: both: earlier = two-vehicle teaching, later = Mahāyāna; Cháng Bǎi: shallow illness is affliction-obstruction, deep illness cognitive obstruction; Miào Jìng: treating cognitive obstruction with Hīnayāna doesn't fit — unwilling to turn to the great
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the earlier medicine is the two-vehicle teaching, the later the Mahāyāna; the shallow illness is affliction-obstruction, the deep one cognitive obstruction. Venerable Miào Jìng: treating the illness of cognitive obstruction with Hīnayāna teaching doesn't fit — these are followers unwilling to turn from small to great.

quiz.q: "The first illness cured, another arises" — what is the other illness, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the affliction-obstruction is removed, but the cognitive-obstruction illness remains
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the affliction-obstruction has been removed, but the illness of cognitive obstruction remains — only the Mahāyāna medicine of selflessness of phenomena removes it.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas with pure faith ride the Buddha's teaching like what?
options: an unsurpassed dharma-vehicle, a wondrously adorned chariot complete in every part, driven by a skilled driver swiftly, without delay
quiz.why: Riding the Buddha's teaching is like an unsurpassed vehicle, a wondrously adorned chariot complete in every part; like a skilled driver, advancing swiftly without delay. Master Cháng Bǎi: lacking one wheel, the cart cannot turn smoothly; not being satisfied with little is "advancing swiftly without delay."

quiz.q: "Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas with pure faith have no doubt about the Buddha's words." What do the lectures say about noble śrāvakas and the Mahāyāna?
options: Cháng Bǎi: arhats fully accept the Buddha and the Mahāyāna — denying it denies the two vehicles too; Miào Jìng: stream-enterers to arhats definitely believe in it — because of wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: arhats never deny the Buddha — they fully accept the Buddha and the Mahāyāna; saying the Mahāyāna isn't the Buddha's word denies the two vehicles too, for without a buddha how could they exist? Venerable Miào Jìng: those with the four fruits definitely believe in the Mahāyāna — because of wisdom.

quiz.q: What is the first of the five truly astonishing qualities?
options: affection towards beings without prior connection
quiz.why: "First, feeling affection towards beings without any prior connection." Venerable Miào Jìng: not because they are my father or mother. Master Cháng Bǎi: from the first resolve the bodhisattva takes all beings as family.

quiz.q: What is the first "not astonishing" quality?
options: taking the suffering of benefiting others as one's own happiness, constantly undergoing it
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas take the suffering from benefiting others as their own happiness, and so constantly undergo it." Venerable Miào Jìng: suffering among beings is ordinary — but not tiring of it and finding joy in it is astonishing. Master Cháng Bǎi: like loving parents for whom any hardship for their children is sweet.

quiz.q: The third quality — "though knowing the taste of silent bliss, constantly teaching." What stage, according to the lectures?
options: both: the ninth ground of unobstructed understanding; Cháng Bǎi also cites Zhiyi: "leading a community too early, harming myself to help others, I only reached the iron wheel"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this refers to bodhisattvas abiding in unobstructed understanding — the ninth ground; he cites Zhiyi's words: "I hoped to reach the copper wheel, but leading a community too early, harming myself to benefit others, I reached only the iron wheel." Venerable Miào Jìng: the ninth ground, Good Wisdom.

quiz.q: The third mark — "equanimity joined with love for an only child." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: with two sons one might favour one; love for an only child has no such partiality
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: with two sons one might treat one better, the other worse — love for an only child has no such unevenness. Master Cháng Bǎi: as the sūtras say, the Buddha regards all beings equally as Rāhula.
